title: Declarative finite spatial vector and extent-inequality composition
benchmark: Development-visible StepGame and SpaRP property regimes

independentExamples.description: Three nonce objects linked by two declared integer displacement vectors require vector addition and sign classification; an unrelated component must not affect the result.
independentExamples.expectedBehavior: Return the declaratively named output class and an ordered replayable edge path.

independentExamples.description: Three renamed extended objects separated along two renamed dimensions require transitive boundary inequalities while overlap on an unmentioned dimension must not fabricate separation.
independentExamples.expectedBehavior: Return only relations whose endpoint inequalities have an explicit graph path, with one witness per relation.

inputTypes: typed vector facts and relation query
typed multi-relation extent facts and relation query
outputTypes: inequality path witness per output relation
preconditions: all dimensions, relation identifiers, vectors, polarities, facts, and endpoints validate
the task declares exact summation, opposed-step invalidation, or orthogonal-overlap policy explicitly
facts, entities, dimensions, graph edges, and path depth remain within core per-task bounds
invariants: core control flow never branches on benchmark, dataset, row, hash, expected answer, or source relation vocabulary
inverse vector traversal is derived from declared vectors
extent output is emitted only when the matching endpoint inequality is reachable
disconnected distractors cannot enter a query witness
every solved result is independently replayable from the accepted task
uncertaintySemantics: Disconnected endpoints are UNKNOWN; insufficient qualitative or extent evidence is UNDERDETERMINED; incompatible constraints are INCONSISTENT_CONTEXT; undeclared output signatures are NO_APPLICABLE_METHOD; bound exhaustion is RESOURCE_LIMIT; malformed tasks are UNPARSED.
proofBehavior: Vector results contain the exact ordered edges used to reconstruct the displacement state. Extent results contain one ordered inequality path for every returned relation. Separate verifiers rebuild the accepted task, replay the paths, and reject omitted, duplicated, altered, or unsupported witnesses.

resourceBounds.datasetPolicy: These are per-example execution bounds. Source adapters stream every source row and never reject a dataset file because of byte size.

kbMigration: none; vector systems and extent systems are passed as validated declarative task metadata, and no source fact is installed in the generic core

guardianControls.valueRenaming: declarative vectors and polarities map to nonce output values
guardianControls.ordering: fact reversal preserves results while query reversal changes direction
guardianControls.negativeControls: mixed-direction extent chain abstains; incompatible cycles fail; bounded paths do not search past policy

remainingGap: This earlier checkpoint did not cover PS1. The later generic method, complete development evidence, and promoted descriptor are recorded in core-change-proposal-ps1.json and development-result.json.
